reviewer: Fresh independent reviewer; single reviewer, no delegation
summary: The exact candidate preserves the accepted startup design and is proportionate to F01. No concrete critical, high, or medium finding. Independent macOS CPU acceptance passed 43 cooperative cases on Python 3.13.16 and 3.14.8, and all five required containment cases on 3.14. Both real 2/6-sample socket rounds trained separate clients, matched actual received payloads, satisfied the numerical weighted reference, and ended naturally without watchdog intervention. The candidate remains subject to root integration and the existing Phase 1C handoff.

candidate.production_scope: Only plato/client.py and base server imports/run/start changed: 326 additions and 124 deletions. Remaining additions are four test helpers/suite and the validation artifact. No manifest, lock, algorithm, training, transport, os._exit, or spawn-policy changes.

production: plato/servers/base.py (complete exact diff; run/start, spawn, periodic, disconnect and close context)

inspected.installed_api: Inspected the installed asyncio Runner initialization/run/close and aiohttp run_app/cancellation implementation. These local installed sources are direct evidence of the versions tested.

retained_implementer_evidence.baseline_red: Reviewed seven retained fresh 3.14 bootstrap failures with exact missing-current-loop sites, seven 3.13 controls, active-failure RED evidence, and the corrected precedence regression. These RED subprocesses were not independently rerun.
retained_implementer_evidence.existing_suites: Verified retained logs/JUnit hashes: each interpreter has 248 existing tests passed, three explicitly unqualified Nanochat skips and eight existing fork warnings. Did not repeat the entire existing suite.
retained_implementer_evidence.final_startup_campaign: Verified 43 cooperative, four teardown, and positive/stalled socket partitions per interpreter. The positive socket repeat is not counted as another unique case; final coverage is 48 unique cases. Historical failed development runs are explicitly separate.

assessments.basis: Local loop/task context managers serve only the existing startup call sites. Monitoring retains the periodic/edge task and a borrowed client's main task. No global exception handler, task factory, child supervisor, AppRunner rewrite, or new configuration/API framework.

get_running_loop rejects nested entry before entrypoint factories/configure/coroutines; get_event_loop conservatively borrows an open current loop. A missing or closed registration selects fresh ownership. Runner is initialized before ordinary-client construction/configure only on the owned path. Borrowed clients and returning/raising server overrides leave current registration, pending caller resources and executor usable. Fresh 3.13 policy-provided loops are deliberately borrowed rather than inferred to be owned.

Server configure and self.start() remain synchronous with unchanged dispatch/signatures. Central/ordinary launch, seed order and spawn policy are preserved. Edge factories, trainer factory and port dispatch remain synchronous; edge uses the shared loop and still adds no server.run periodic task. Real base.start consumes even a supplied loop through aiohttp's existing close contract.

The actual coroutine receives the post-configure ContextVar values through copy_context on the Runner path and normal task context on the borrowed path. Real entrypoint tests reject client.run, Server.run and Server.start inside a running loop before factory/configure/Socket.IO creation. No fresh-start test installs an open loop to make raw bootstrap pass; explicit absent, closed and borrowed registrations are separate compatibility cases.

Independent configure/start/on_startup/bind errors take precedence over managed active failures and teardown diagnostics. Only the recorded monitor stop plus the actual BaseEventLoop.run_until_complete stop-check traceback replaces the specific loop-stopped RuntimeError; an independent same-text RuntimeError survives. Secondary failures include task identity and notes where applicable. KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit retain control-flow identity and exit behavior.

Completed task exceptions are retrieved. Positive public Task.cancelling() classifies cancellation-finalizer exceptions as teardown without stopping aiohttp cleanup. Local cleanup disarms the monitor and does not issue another cancellation to an already-awaiting finalizer. Real aiohttp periodic and edge active failures reach the synchronous caller; mixed setup/finalizer/sibling cases preserve setup failure while the sibling finishes.

Full fallback cancellation/generator/executor cleanup is limited to an explicitly created open loop. Borrowed scopes join only their retained startup task. Closed aiohttp loops are not finalized again; closed registrations are not restored. Owned Runner and server fallback tests demonstrate cooperative task/generator/executor finalization on success/error, including repeat invocation. Independent final inspection found no live recorded process identity and successfully bound/listened on every recorded port.

Actual FedAvg server.run spawns two real simple clients with real basic/composable SGD, separate 2/6-sample TensorDatasets, comm_simulation=false, normal processors/serialization/socket chunks and unmodified aggregation. Callback observations own copies before later model mutation and match actual logical IDs, including reassignment. Both clients change parameters, actual decoded payloads equal independently trained weights, and both clients return naturally.

Dedicated subprocess sessions, PID/create-time identities, durable child-start observations, output draining and bounded TERM/KILL/reaping distinguish natural success from containment. All five repeated negative cases are explicitly timed out and forced, with no survivors. Stalled-client parent exit code zero does not pass a round: no aggregate exists, only one payload is processed, and the child requires TERM. No forced termination is counted as successful runtime cleanup or primary-error delivery.

independent_acceptance.independent_numerical_method: Recomputed every floating parameter from independently read result.json using ordinary Python floats and math.fsum: W0 + sum(n_i * (W_i - W0))/sum(n_i). Maximum absolute error was 1.4901161193847656e-08 for both interpreters.

limitations: Natural cleanup remains cooperative. Runner/aiohttp cancellation gathers and async-generator finalizers can stall; Runner executor shutdown can wait up to 300 seconds. The five-second fallback executor timeout bounds waiting and does not kill a running thread. This is the accepted design limitation, not a new production supervision requirement.
The four teardown negatives and stalled-client negative prove watchdog containment only. They do not prove graceful cleanup or delivery of the original exception to the caller.
Production os._exit on the successful real round proves transport/training/aggregation and natural process disappearance, not Python finally execution; separate cooperative tests cover finalization.

The independent reviewer repeated containment only on 3.14, and reviewed the implementer's hash-verified 3.13 containment records. The existing 248-test suites were inspected, not independently rerun.

Three existing Nanochat skips remain unqualified until Phase 1C initializes source/prerequisites. Eight existing fork warnings and runtime/containment marker registration and Linux CI duration qualification remain with Phase 1C; no unrelated repair or dependency reopening is required here.
Python 3.13 remains the selected default. Python 3.14 evidence is core startup/CPU forward compatibility on this macOS host, not optional robotics, MLX, Nanochat, or Linux support qualification.
